scope_note: Lightweight Gate A screening only. No exhaustive licensing audit, no measured 91-country coverage audit, and no production approval.

fact_estimate_legend.VERIFIED_FROM_USER_SEARCH_SPACE: Criterion construct is taken from the supplied 84-item search space.
fact_estimate_legend.VERIFIED_WHERE_CITED: A cited official/primary page confirms that the publisher or dataset family exists and supports the stated scope/freshness fact.
fact_estimate_legend.PRELIMINARY_ESTIMATE: Fit, comparability, stable-universe coverage, licensing fit, and priority remain hypotheses for Phase 3C unless explicitly stated otherwise.

E01.claim: UNESCO UIS describes itself as the official source of cross-nationally comparable education data; its browser offers APIs, bulk downloads, metadata, and a February 2026 release.

E02.claim: ILOSTAT provides bulk/API-style access to harmonised labour indicators, dictionaries, metadata, and modelled estimates.

E03.claim: UN DESA International Migrant Stock 2024 covers 233 countries and areas for 1990–2024, but many 2024 values are extrapolations rather than full reassessments.

E04.claim: WHO Global Health Observatory exposes country and indicator data through an OData API.

E05.claim: ITU DataHub contains hundreds of ICT indicators and data for nearly 200 economies, including access, use, coverage, affordability, and quality-of-service indicators.

E06.claim: WHO/UNICEF JMP's 2025 household WASH release reports estimates through 2024.

E07.claim: World Bank WGI 2025 reports six annual governance dimensions for more than 200 economies through 2024 and publishes uncertainty; it is a perception-based composite.

E08.claim: World Bank WBL 2026 covers 190 economies, is current to 1 October 2025, and its catalog records CC BY 4.0.

E09.claim: World Bank ICP 2021 has observed results for 176 economies plus imputed results for 19; it provides PPPs and price-level indexes.

E10.claim: IMF WEO April 2026 includes inflation, unemployment, growth, fiscal and external indicators and is published twice yearly, with some country-series gaps.

E11.claim: OECD Taxing Wages 2026 reports effective tax wedges for 38 member countries and selected household cases, well below the 91-country universe.

E12.claim: World Bank CCKP offers country, subnational, watershed and gridded climate data, including API access and World Bank dataset terms.

E13.claim: Copernicus ERA5 is a globally complete, consistent reanalysis from 1940 onward with continuing updates.

E14.claim: EU/JRC INFORM Risk 2026 is openly downloadable with source data and calculation steps for global country risk.

E15.claim: ILO NATLEX/NORMLEX provide large official corpora of national labour and social-security legislation, but not a ready-made relocation score.

E16.claim: ILGA World's 2024 Laws on Us covers 11 LGBTQ+ legal categories but is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0.

E17.claim: World Happiness Report 2026 uses harmonised Gallup life-evaluation responses averaged over 2023–2025 and makes the published three-year averages downloadable.

E18.claim: World Bank Logistics Performance Index 2023 is an official cross-country measure of trade-logistics speed and reliability.

criteria.name: Overall higher-education opportunity
criteria.measures: National breadth, participation, completion and credible quality signals in tertiary education.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Quality is not captured by availability alone; rankings are commercially licensed and institution-weighted.

criteria.name: Technology and engineering education
criteria.measures: Strength and availability of tertiary programmes and graduates in engineering, ICT and related fields.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Global field-of-study counts are plausible, but comparable programme quality and institution location are not.

criteria.name: Medical and health-sciences education
criteria.measures: Availability and quality of medicine, dentistry, nursing, pharmacy and allied-health education.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Programme quality, recognition and seat access vary by profession and institution; WDOMS is not a quality ranking.

criteria.name: Business, commerce, and management education
criteria.measures: Availability and quality of business, finance, economics, accounting and management education.
likely_dataset_or_indicator_families: AACSB/EQUIS and subject rankings for discovery
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Accreditation and rankings cover a selective institution set and carry licensing and selection bias.

criteria.name: Research and innovation ecosystem
criteria.measures: National research intensity, outputs, patents, doctoral capacity and university–industry links.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: A composite must avoid mixing inputs and outputs or importing opaque GII weights.

criteria.name: International-student accessibility
criteria.measures: Practical accessibility for international students: enrolment openness, English-taught options, visas and support.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Mobility stock is comparable; admissions, English-taught programmes and visa rules need manual current-policy coding.

criteria.name: Tuition affordability
criteria.measures: Tuition cost faced by representative domestic/international students relative to income or PPP.
likely_authoritative_publisher_families: national ministries and institution fee schedules
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Fees vary by institution, programme, residency and scholarship; global harmonised international-student prices are unlikely.

criteria.name: School education quality
criteria.measures: Primary/secondary learning outcomes, completion and system quality.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Administrative completion is broad, but common learning assessments miss many stable-universe countries and cycles.

criteria.name: International-school availability
criteria.measures: Availability and affordability of recognised international schools in likely destinations.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: A city-level institution inventory and commercial-directory licensing would be required.

criteria.name: Recognition and portability of qualifications
criteria.measures: Ease of academic/professional recognition and portability of foreign qualifications.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Outcome depends on origin, destination, qualification and profession; no single country score is defensible.

criteria.name: Overall job-market opportunity
criteria.measures: National employment opportunity using employment, unemployment, participation and labour-underutilisation signals.
likely_dataset_or_indicator_families: ILOSTAT modelled estimates and harmonised labour-force indicators
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Vacancies are not globally comparable, so the first version should stay with harmonised labour outcomes.

criteria.name: Software and technology jobs
criteria.measures: Depth of software, ICT, data, AI and cybersecurity employment.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Global occupation aggregates are broad; granular tech vacancies are platform-dependent and concentrated in cities.

criteria.name: Medical and healthcare jobs
criteria.measures: Demand and employment opportunity for health professionals, separate from licensing access.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Provider shortage is not equivalent to accessible jobs, and licensing must remain a separate gate.

criteria.name: Business, finance, and professional-services jobs
criteria.measures: Demand for finance, consulting, accounting, marketing, operations, sales and management roles.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Occupational groupings are broad and vacancy data are uneven; major-city concentration is material.

criteria.name: Engineering and skilled technical jobs
criteria.measures: Demand for civil, mechanical, electrical, industrial, energy and skilled technical roles.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Broad ISCO groups are comparable, but specialisms, licensing and regional projects are not.

criteria.name: Entrepreneurship and startup opportunity
criteria.measures: Business formation, firm entry, startup activity, finance access and survival conditions.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Startup funding/activity sources often have selective coverage or commercial terms; formation counts are not survival quality.

criteria.name: Average earning potential
criteria.measures: Representative gross/net earnings, ideally occupation- and cost-adjusted.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: National averages mask occupation, tax and city-cost differences; net pay requires household scenarios.

criteria.name: Income growth and career mobility
criteria.measures: Wage growth, promotion prospects and occupational mobility over time.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Promotion and mobility require longitudinal microdata that are not globally harmonised or broadly reusable.

criteria.name: Employment protection and worker rights
criteria.measures: Formal and effective protection on hours, leave, dismissal, bargaining and core labour rights.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Law, ratification and enforcement are distinct; comparable coding requires current legal review.

criteria.name: Remote-work suitability
criteria.measures: Digital and legal practicality of remote work, including connectivity, visas, coworking and time-zone fit.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: It overlaps internet and visas, while time zone and legal fit depend on employer and user origin.

criteria.name: Personal income-tax burden
criteria.measures: Effective personal income-tax burden for representative income and household cases.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: OECD's comparable effective-tax model covers only 38 countries; global extension requires maintained official-rule coding.

criteria.name: Social-security and mandatory contribution burden
criteria.measures: Employee/employer payroll, pension and other compulsory contribution burden.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Global comparability is constrained by ceilings, benefit entitlements and the same OECD coverage limit.

criteria.name: Consumption and indirect-tax burden
criteria.measures: VAT/GST/sales-tax rates and household exposure to indirect taxation.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Headline rates are broad but effective burden needs country-specific exemptions and household consumption baskets.

criteria.name: Overall affordability
criteria.measures: Relative household-consumption price level against a common benchmark.
likely_dataset_or_indicator_families: ICP household-consumption PPP and price-level indexes
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Already represented in Konsider; retain as an existing monitor, not a new Phase 3 research target.

criteria.name: Housing affordability
criteria.measures: Rent/home-price burden relative to income and availability in likely migrant destinations.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: High decision value justifies strategic research, but a national average is misleading and global city rent data are often commercial.

criteria.name: Healthcare affordability
criteria.measures: Out-of-pocket spending, insurance burden and financial-protection risk.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Aggregate out-of-pocket shares do not describe immigrant eligibility, premiums or point-of-care prices.

criteria.name: Childcare and family-cost burden
criteria.measures: Childcare fees and other recurring family costs for representative households.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Fees depend on age, city, income, subsidies and immigration status; OECD-style comparisons do not approach global coverage.

criteria.name: Savings and disposable-income potential
criteria.measures: Net income remaining after taxes and essential household costs.
likely_authoritative_publisher_families: Derived from approved earnings, tax, housing, health and childcare components
criteria.downgrade_rationale: This is a profile-derived composite with shared inputs and scenario weights, not an independent criterion.

criteria.name: Currency and macroeconomic stability
criteria.measures: Inflation, exchange-rate volatility and broad macro/sovereign stability.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: A transparent small indicator set is preferable to a proprietary sovereign-risk composite.

criteria.name: Existing immigrant share
criteria.measures: International migrant or foreign-born stock as a share of resident population.
likely_dataset_or_indicator_families: International Migrant Stock 2024 total destination and population denominator
criteria.downgrade_rationale: The source mixes country-of-birth and citizenship definitions and many 2024 values are extrapolated.

criteria.name: Immigrant community depth
criteria.measures: Size, origin diversity and local concentration of established migrant communities.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Origin-specific usefulness and city concentration make a single national diversity score weak.

criteria.name: Skilled-work visa accessibility
criteria.measures: Accessibility of skilled-worker routes under a fixed worker profile and policy date.
likely_dataset_or_indicator_families: Official visa statutes, occupation lists, salary thresholds, quotas, processing guidance
criteria.downgrade_rationale: No global ready-made dataset; eligibility depends on occupation, salary, origin, sponsor and changing rules.

criteria.name: Permanent-residency accessibility
criteria.measures: Time, eligibility and predictability of permanent residence under defined scenarios.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: PR eligibility is route-, origin- and family-dependent and needs maintained legal coding.

criteria.name: Citizenship accessibility
criteria.measures: Time and restrictions for naturalisation, including dual citizenship and tests.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Formal law is codable, but discretion, residence counting and policy updates complicate a scalar score.

criteria.name: Post-study migration pathway
criteria.measures: Ability of international graduates to stay, work and transition after study.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Pathways depend on credential level, institution, occupation and policy date.

criteria.name: Family reunification support
criteria.measures: Ability to sponsor spouses, children, parents and other dependants.
likely_dataset_or_indicator_families: Official family-reunification statutes, sponsor thresholds, waiting periods and dependant work rights
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Family definitions, income thresholds and sponsor status differ materially; parent sponsorship is especially non-comparable.

criteria.name: Government stance toward immigrants
criteria.measures: Formal immigration-policy direction, integration supports and stability of migrant access.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: It conflates policy intent, rights, implementation and attitudes; leading indexes have limited coverage or licensing uncertainty.

criteria.name: Professional-licensing accessibility for immigrants
criteria.measures: Ease of foreign-qualification recognition and entry to a specified regulated profession.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Origin, profession, credential and language dependence prevent a universal score; deep research should test scenario templates.

criteria.name: Visa and immigration processing efficiency
criteria.measures: Transparency, speed and predictability of visa/immigration administration.
likely_dataset_or_indicator_families: Official service standards and processing-time dashboards
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Published clocks use different case types and exclude paused/incomplete cases; rejection rates reflect applicant mix.

criteria.name: English usability
criteria.measures: Extent to which work, education, health, government and daily life can be navigated in English.
criteria.likely_freshness: SLOW_STRUCTURAL: census plus current legal status
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Commercial proficiency rankings are not enough; usability varies strongly by city and domain.

criteria.name: Local-language difficulty and learning burden
criteria.measures: User-specific burden of learning and needing the local language.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Difficulty depends on the user's known languages, profession and destination; no universal direction exists.

criteria.name: Social inclusion and acceptance of immigrants
criteria.measures: Surveyed acceptance of immigrants, discrimination experience and social trust.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Global surveys differ in years and samples, and small states are often absent; lived experience varies locally.

criteria.name: Cultural openness and diversity
criteria.measures: Religious, ethnic, cultural and lifestyle diversity and practical openness.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: The construct mixes diversity, tolerance and freedom; direction and weights are contestable and city effects large.

criteria.name: Gender equality
criteria.measures: Legal and economic equality for women.
likely_authoritative_publisher_families: World Bank Women, Business and the Law
likely_dataset_or_indicator_families: WBL 2026 legal, supportive-framework and enforcement-perception pillars
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Already represented in Konsider; monitor the verified WBL source rather than duplicate research.

criteria.name: LGBTQ+ legal and social inclusion
criteria.measures: Legal protection, recognition and safety for LGBTQ+ people.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: ILGA has strong scope but its 2024 report is CC BY-NC; social acceptance/safety needs separate survey evidence.

criteria.name: Violent-crime and homicide safety
criteria.measures: Intentional-homicide risk, with broader violence only where genuinely comparable.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Homicide is already represented; reported violent crime should not be appended without comparability evidence.

criteria.name: Property-crime and everyday safety
criteria.measures: Day-to-day risk of theft, burglary, robbery, fraud and victimisation.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Recorded crime is dominated by reporting/legal differences; globally harmonised victim surveys and city coverage are sparse.

criteria.name: Political stability and civil peace
criteria.measures: Conflict, political violence, unrest and continuity of normal civic life.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: WGI is perception-based and conflict-event data may have licensing or reporting asymmetries.

criteria.name: Rule of law and institutional trust
criteria.measures: Rule of law, corruption control, judicial confidence and institutional performance.
likely_dataset_or_indicator_families: WGI Rule of Law/Control of Corruption/Government Effectiveness
criteria.downgrade_rationale: WGI is a composite of perceptions with margins of error; institutional trust is not identical to rule of law.

criteria.name: Healthcare system capacity and quality
criteria.measures: Health-service capacity, coverage and quality using workforce, service and outcome indicators.
likely_dataset_or_indicator_families: WHO GHO/UHC service coverage, workforce and beds
criteria.downgrade_rationale: No single indicator captures access, quality and waiting time; mixed years and modelled values are likely.

criteria.name: Emergency-care readiness
criteria.measures: Ambulance access, trauma/emergency capacity and response readiness.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Global emergency-care assessments are sparse and national averages cannot represent response time.

criteria.name: Air pollution
criteria.measures: Population-weighted exposure to ambient PM2.5.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Already represented in Konsider; city exposure may be a later layer but not a duplicate national criterion.

criteria.name: Water quality and sanitation
criteria.measures: Safely managed drinking water/sanitation access and related service quality.
likely_dataset_or_indicator_families: JMP safely managed drinking water, sanitation and hygiene
criteria.downgrade_rationale: JMP access is broad, but continuity, taste/contaminants and migrant-city reliability are separate constructs.

criteria.name: Food safety and public-health protection
criteria.measures: Strength of food regulation, inspection and outbreak prevention/response.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Inputs and outbreak counts reflect surveillance capacity; comparable inspection-performance data are fragmented.

criteria.name: Mental-health support
criteria.measures: Availability, affordability and acceptability of mental-health services.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Provider counts do not measure affordability or stigma, and access is local with substantial missingness.

criteria.name: Electricity access and reliability
criteria.measures: Household electricity access plus outage frequency/duration and reliability.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Access is near-global, but outage metrics lack harmonised 90% coverage; current experimental composite overlaps access.

criteria.name: Water-supply reliability
criteria.measures: Continuity, shortage risk and resilience of household/urban water supply.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: JMP access does not ensure 24/7 supply; utility-level continuity is not globally standardised.

criteria.name: Internet access, speed, and reliability
criteria.measures: Internet adoption, mobile/fixed coverage, performance, affordability and reliability.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: ITU access/coverage is broad, but speed/outage measures may be commercial or incomplete; avoid duplicating the existing composite.

criteria.name: Transport and logistics infrastructure
criteria.measures: Road, rail, port, airport and trade-logistics performance.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: LPI has limited country coverage and is perception-based; a broad composite would overlap existing infrastructure readiness.

criteria.name: Urban public transport
criteria.measures: Coverage, affordability, safety and reliability of public transport in destination cities.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Country scores are invalid; a fixed city universe and reusable feed policy are prerequisites.

criteria.name: International connectivity
criteria.measures: Direct-flight access, airport connectivity and travel time to relevant origins/centres.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Route schedules are city/airport and origin-specific; comprehensive timetable data are usually commercial.

criteria.name: Digital-government readiness
criteria.measures: Availability and maturity of online services, digital ID and digital public administration.
likely_dataset_or_indicator_families: UN E-Government Development Index/Online Service Index
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Composite editions and weights require sensitivity review; user experience can diverge from formal availability.

criteria.name: Infrastructure readiness composite
criteria.measures: Combined digital and logistics readiness.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Already available experimentally; Phase 3 should research its components rather than duplicate the composite.

criteria.name: Temperature comfort
criteria.measures: Climatological heat, cold, humidity and seasonal exposure at likely destinations.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Global data are excellent, but national averages are misleading and comfort has no universal direction.

criteria.name: Climate preference fit
criteria.measures: Match between a user's preferred warm/cold/dry/humid/four-season climate and destination conditions.
likely_dataset_or_indicator_families: Derived preference model over ERA5/CCKP temperature, precipitation and humidity
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Data coverage is strong, but this belongs in a transparent preference model, not a higher-is-better criterion.

criteria.name: Extreme-weather risk
criteria.measures: Exposure to heatwaves, floods, storms, wildfire, drought and severe cold.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Hazard components have different scales and city exposure; avoid double counting vulnerability/coping capacity.

criteria.name: Long-term climate-change exposure
criteria.measures: Future physical exposure to sea-level rise, heat/water stress and ecosystem pressures.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Results depend on scenario, horizon, model ensemble and population exposure assumptions.

criteria.name: Natural-disaster risk
criteria.measures: Expected loss/exposure from geophysical and weather-related natural hazards.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Overlaps extreme-weather risk; geophysical hazards should be separable and composite weights tested.

criteria.name: Environmental quality beyond PM2.5
criteria.measures: Waste, water pollution, green space, noise, biodiversity and other environmental conditions.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: The construct is too broad, city-sensitive and dependent on composite weighting; EPI licensing must be checked.

criteria.name: Climate resilience and adaptation readiness
criteria.measures: Institutional and infrastructure capacity to adapt to and recover from climate shocks.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Readiness indexes are composite/modelled and overlap governance, infrastructure and disaster risk.

criteria.name: Work-life balance
criteria.measures: Working hours, paid leave, parental leave and commute burden.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Leave law is not take-up; commute is city-level and survey coverage is weak, so start with hours/leave components.

criteria.name: Family friendliness
criteria.measures: Family-support environment spanning leave, childcare, schools, safety and recreation.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: This is best as a transparent family profile assembled from approved components, not a new opaque dataset.

criteria.name: Quality of urban life
criteria.measures: Urban public space, walkability, cleanliness, congestion, amenities and design.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Requires a city universe, geospatial methodology and multiple sources with uneven licensing.

criteria.name: Recreation, culture, and leisure
criteria.measures: Access to sports, arts, libraries, dining, nature and community activity.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Amenity value is preference-based, highly local and usually reliant on commercial or volunteered POI data.

criteria.name: Religious freedom and freedom of expression
criteria.measures: Formal and practical religious freedom, expression and civic participation.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Legal guarantees and lived freedom diverge; prominent indices mix expert judgments and may have reuse restrictions.

criteria.name: Social protection and welfare support
criteria.measures: Eligibility and adequacy of unemployment, pension, disability and family benefits.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Benefit access and value depend on contributions, residence, immigration status and household scenario.

criteria.name: Retirement suitability
criteria.measures: Combined suitability for older migrants: health, cost, pensions, residency, safety and lifestyle.
likely_dataset_or_indicator_families: Profile composite plus official retirement-residence rules
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Overlaps C84 and combines incompatible profile inputs; retain only one retirement profile after component approval.

criteria.name: Overall life satisfaction
criteria.measures: Average self-reported life evaluation of residents.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: The measure is comparable but misses some small states, is an outcome rather than an actionable lever, and Gallup reuse terms need audit.

criteria.name: Suitability for a software professional
criteria.measures: Profile score for a software professional using jobs, pay, tax, English, visas and ecosystem.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Explicit profile composite; no independent source search is warranted.

criteria.name: Suitability for a medical professional
criteria.measures: Profile score for a medical professional using demand, licensing, language, pay and visas.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Explicit profession/profile composite; research its components instead.

criteria.name: Suitability for a student
criteria.measures: Student profile score using education, tuition, access, safety and post-study routes.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Explicit profile composite; no independent criterion dataset exists.

criteria.name: Suitability for a family with school-age children
criteria.measures: Family-with-children profile score using schools, safety, health, housing and migration rules.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Explicit household profile; component evidence and weights must remain visible.

criteria.name: Suitability for an entrepreneur
criteria.measures: Entrepreneur profile score using formation, finance, tax, immigration, markets and digital government.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Explicit profile composite; research component criteria rather than seek a single index.

criteria.name: Suitability for retirement
criteria.measures: Retiree profile score using health, affordability, climate, residency, safety and life quality.
criteria.downgrade_rationale: Explicit preference/profile composite and duplicate of C77's intended decision.
